what_its_for: Albendazole is an antiparasitic medicine used to treat certain worm infections. It works by killing or stopping the growth of parasites inside your body. It is commonly used to treat tapeworm infections (such as neurocysticercosis and cystic hydatid disease), but your doctor may prescribe it for other types of worm infections as well.
how_to_take: Take albendazole by mouth with food, preferably a fatty meal (such as one that contains cheese, butter, or milk), as this helps your body absorb the medicine better. Swallow the tablet whole, or you may crush or chew it and swallow it with water if needed. Try to take it at the same time each day. Do not stop taking it early unless your doctor tells you to, even if you feel better.
dosing: Your dose depends on your weight, the type of infection you have, and your age. A common adult dose is 400 mg taken twice a day (morning and evening) with meals. Treatment may last from a few days to several months depending on your condition. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose without asking your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store albendazole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice while taking albendazole, as it may increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Do not drink alcohol excessively, as it may affect your liver. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during treatment and for at least 3 days after your last dose. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have blurred vision.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: severe stomach pain, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, unusual tiredness or weakness, fever, unusual bruising or bleeding, severe headache, vision changes or seizures, or a skin rash. These could be signs of serious side effects including liver problems or low blood cell counts. Call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse during treatment.
when_it_works: Albendazole starts working right away, but you may not notice improvement in your symptoms immediately. For some infections, it can take several days to a few weeks before you feel better. For more serious infections like cysts, treatment may take months, and improvement may be gradual. Keep taking the medicine for the full prescribed duration even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use albendazole if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause birth defects. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 days after stopping. If you become pregnant during treatment, tell your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding: It is not known if albendazole passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. Children: Dosing in children is based on body weight. Children under 6 years old should use this medicine only under close medical supervision. Liver problems: This medicine may not be safe if you have liver disease. Your doctor will monitor your liver function with blood tests during treatment. Elderly patients: Use with caution; your doctor will decide if any dose adjustments are needed.
